answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to stake a deposit earned through verified work, not just created accounts. A newcomer must complete a long voyage of useful, checkable tasks before gaining full trading rights, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive in time and compute. Even at the nadir of trust, when a new agent is unknown, its stake can be slashed if it misbehaves, while honest agents keep building reputation. Like timber that must be seasoned before it bears weight, reputation should only mature slowly, making mass forgery unprofitable.
